summary: In this lesson, students will learn to explain the need of searching for solutions creatively for any challenge or problem for success in life. They will negotiate a solution, create a shared civic artifact, and review another group's proposal. The lesson will be conducted through role-play, debate, and jigsaw activities.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Students will be assessed based on their participation and engagement in the activities, as well as the quality of their shared civic artifact and presentation.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Students will reflect on their learning and share their thoughts with the class.
selected_activity:
Activity: Citizen Charter / Wall Newspaper Poster: Competency Level 8.5.2
Approach: Students use citizen charter / wall newspaper poster to explore 'Explains the need of searching for solutions creatively for any challenge or problem for success in life.'. Students negotiate a solution, create a shared civic artifact, and review another group's proposal. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students negotiate a solution, create a shared civic artifact, and review another group's proposal. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 40 students using 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A group civic proposal, diagram, or public information message.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
